ambiguities.statement: Many seams name multiple primary owners or unordered owner sets without deterministic precedence when their contracts disagree.
Labels such as stale consumer, owner-gap, stale/inconsistent, aligned owner, hybrid, residual stale scope, and structurally unreliable have no defined severity, gate effect, or completion state.
GATE-010 cannot express required routing and command-normalization checks, but the index does not say whether affected progression is blocked, advisory, or temporarily accepted.

Line 228 makes generated governance seal-phase-only, line 256 permits metadata-only index and governance registration to refresh the same artifacts after stability, and context line 274 again separates index refresh from seal-only artifacts; the exact authorized transition is unclear.
“Subscription-first” coexists with Gemini Direct being direct-key-only/API-key-backed; requested/effective route resolution and fallback precedence are not explicit here.
The Plan Compile tab and node-factory UX are visible while PlanCompile and launch remain disabled; whether controls are hidden, disabled, demonstrative, or actionable is unstated.

Governance artifacts are called metadata-only/registering outputs even though they include Spec Lock, shards, evidence, graph, and decisions; the boundary between metadata registration and authoritative governance mutation is unclear.
Packaged receipts are user-visible evidence but not runtime truth, while the window does not identify the runtime-truth authority or freshness/provenance signal presented beside them.

builder_discretion.statement: A builder could invent precedence among multiple primary owners because no tie-breaker is given locally.
A builder could silently consume or ignore stale, owner-gap, or unreliable documents because those classifications have no fail-closed consequence.
Projection correctness, replay, migration, and storage recovery behavior would require invention unless owner persistence contracts close the gaps.
Provider/account fallback, credential lifecycle, quota exhaustion, and mid-run identity changes remain locally discretionary.
Backend failover and daemon trust/unavailable behavior remain locally discretionary.
The actor and evidence that declare Plans stable and authorize each governance refresh remain unspecified.
Closure reuse/reopen, duplicate identity, concurrent update, and partial-artifact handling remain locally discretionary.
Runtime enablement authority and truthful disabled GUI behavior remain unspecified despite visible compile/approval surfaces.

claims.statement: Owner documents reconcile before consumers, stale canon cannot remain a peer alternative, and the index routes rather than re-owning behavior; primary owners carry canon while adjacent, stale, and implicated documents are reconciliation companions.

The seam catalog explicitly identifies stale or inconsistent consumers, owner gaps, an owner/consumer hybrid, residual stale scope, duplicated canon, unresolved coordination contradictions, a structurally unreliable Crosswalk, and a GATE layer behind owner contracts.

The rewrite direction is a unified provider event model, canonical seglog event ledger projected to redb and Tantivy, a central tool registry/policy engine with patch-apply-verify-rollback, Rust/Slint GUI backends plus a trusted local daemon, and subscription-first route/account/model-dependent authentication.

Provider/account/promoted-shell ownership is split among Models, usage, Multi-Account/provider docs, promoted-feature spec, Final GUI, Orchestrator, Run Modes, Executor, and storage; stale pre-promotion and recovery-shell wording is lineage or mirror-cleanup input, not live authority.

Bootstrap planning splits ledger, Plan Document, Plan-to-node-readiness, and migration authority; its ledger is source-lineage only, and ordinary ledger/drafting/conversion/index/readiness work must not update Spec Lock, shards, evidence, graph, or auto-decisions.

Semantic closure authority is split between PLS-012 durable registry/reopen semantics and PDS-014 deterministic finding/check identities and matrix validation; workflow/prompts are consumers, and scripts plus audit JSONL artifacts are governance support rather than product execution.

Plans-to-code ownership spans the design-only PlanCompile state machine, automated test policy, Executor intake/preflights/receipts, future Goal approval/completion, six model settings, visible Orchestrator Plan Compile GUI, worktree safety, packaged evidence projection, shared schemas, and readiness/doc-impact scans.

After live Plans stabilize, metadata-only index/governance registration may refresh governance artifacts, but those outputs do not enable PlanCompile, Planning Wizard/Codex launch, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, queues, manifests, implementation, GoalRuns, builds, or dispatch.

The PRD/Planning context assigns intake, projection, approval, planning states, GUI, testing, downstream runtime contracts, schemas, consumer surfaces, and shared envelopes to named owners while declaring a runtime-capable direction that remains launch-disabled and excludes legacy wizard names from active retrieval.

cross_window_seams.statement: Context lines 51-68 establish owner-first reconciliation and introduce the routing guard whose operative catalog fills this window.
The contract/Crosswalk/storage/UI/run/HITL/usage seam family dominates lines 71-195 and carries known stale, gap, precedence, terminology, and duplicate-canon conditions into many owner documents.
Rewrite persistence, tool policy, GUI daemon, and provider auth claims cross rewrite-tie-in, Multi-Account, Prompt Pipeline, usage, Final GUI, and storage owners.
Bootstrap, semantic closure, and Plans-to-code share Planning Ledger, Plan Document, Plan-to-node, governance artifacts, audit matrices, and downstream runtime/readiness boundaries.
The PRD/Planning context continues handoff ownership into runtime-capable but disabled schemas, GUI, commands, events, lineage documents, and governance refresh rules.
The Native Goal Runtime heading begins in context at lines 278-280, but its owner split lies in WIN-00-plans-index-0003.

invalid_reason: Substantive reviewer agent identities were reused across successive window/role assignments, violating the Fresh Agent Isolation Protocol.

negative_space_observations.statement: The routing map lists repeated, stale, inconsistent, owner-gap, and structurally unreliable surfaces without a lifecycle for opening, prioritizing, blocking, resolving, validating, or retiring a seam.

Canonical seglog with redb/Tantivy projections lacks local behavior for crash atomicity, projection lag/divergence, ordering, duplicate events, replay idempotency, corruption, schema migration, rebuild, overload, or partial projection failure.

The tool-policy and patch pipeline omits malicious-tool/provider handling, permission denial, partial apply, verification failure, rollback failure, cancellation, retry limits, concurrent mutation, and recovery ownership.

GUI backends and the trusted daemon lack exact probe/failover/recovery states, daemon authentication/authorization, origin isolation, version negotiation, unavailable behavior, and truthful degraded-state presentation.

Subscription-first and route-specific authentication omit credential acquisition/storage/revocation, requested-to-effective transition rules, account-switch concurrency, quota exhaustion, health degradation, fallback authorization, and audit evidence.
Governance refresh depends on unspecified stability and lacks locking, concurrent-writer, partial-generation, rollback, stale-artifact marking, hash mismatch, and interrupted-seal behavior.

Semantic closure support lacks local handling for concurrent JSONL writes, duplicate finding keys, corrupted rows, subject mutation, stale previously_closed reuse, partial matrix generation, malicious source artifacts, and reopen races.

A visible Plan Compile tab, animated node-factory UX, Planning Wizard Approve And Build ownership, and runtime-capable schemas coexist with disabled runtime, but no disabled-state copy, authority check, enablement transition, double-submit behavior, cancellation, or misleading-success guard is stated.
